notes: **Scope.** Straight line: length of perpendicular from a given point… — Analytic Geometry, Mathematics (class-11-notes).

**Tested.** define it · list: straight line, length of perpendicular from a given point to a given line, bisectors of the angles between two straight lines · one worked example · one misconception each.
**Fact.** Line: point–slope y − y₁ = m(x − x₁); perpendicular distance from (x₁,y₁) to ax+by+c=0 is |ax₁+by₁+c|/√(a²+b²).
**Fact.** Pair of lines: a·S ≡ ax² + 2hxy + by²; represents a real pair iff h² ≥ ab. Angle between: tanθ = 2√(h²−ab)/(a+b).
**Fact.** Homogeneous: ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 (two lines through origin); bisectors: (x² − y²)/(a−b) = xy/h.
**Fact.** Direction cosines of a line: l² + m² + n² = 1; distance between two points in space √(Δx²+Δy²+Δz²).
